notes:
Snapshot: emberlane is a national ecommerce company (fashion + home) running Zendesk + in-house refunds service.

Key needs and constraints:
- Primary: agent assist that can surface refund eligibility and craft API calls to 'payments.refunds.create' and 'orders.update' (idempotent, traceable).
- Must support tool-calling to two systems: Zendesk (ticket update, tags, private note) and internal Refunds API (create/refund/revoke).
- SLOs: agent assist latency (p95) <= 300ms for token-generation + tool-call orchestration; ticket creation/update end-to-end <= 800ms ideally.
- Throughput: 500 requests/sec baseline during peak working hours, spike-ready to 1500 req/sec during promotions (black friday-like events).
- Reliability: guaranteed-at-least-once delivery with dedupe support; auditing of all tool-calls for legal/chargeback investigations.
- Security: strict data residency (US), KMS for keys, SOC2, SSO/SAML with SCIM provisioning.
- Cost sensitivity: medium — willing to pay premium for reliability and predictable pricing during spikes.
- Model preferences: prefer curated open models (Redwood-tested) with quantized variants for Dedicated; want fallback to smaller model for cold starts.

Recent timeline (bullets):
- 2026-01-15: initial inbound via website form, AE Jordan Patel assigned.
- 2026-01-27: discovery call (high-level requirements, attach security doc) — see ff_2026-02-22_emberlane-demo-01.
- 2026-02-22: live demo of Redwood agent-assist with synthetic refund flow. Customer asked: "Can you guarantee no duplicate refunds on retries?" — discussed idempotency tokens and stateful confirmations.
- 2026-02-28: security questionnaire submitted (drive:/security/emberlane-security-questions-2026.pdf).
- 2026-03-04: engineering sync to review refund API contracts and webhook retry behaviour (ff_2026-03-04_toolcaller-sync). Action: AE to provide schema for refunds.create and sample error codes.
- 2026-03-05: Redwood provided estimated architecture for tool-calling (Dedicated nodes + VPC peering).

Open tech/ops details called out by customer:
- Must support synchronous tool-call for agent UI (agent clicks 'refund' -> model suggests amount & reason -> Redwood calls Refunds API -> returns status). Need <1s perceived latency in UI.
- Asynchronous webhook flow for long-running escalations (create escalation ticket, attach artifacts). Retry/backoff policy required; prefer DLQ integration (S3/simple DB) and trace id propagation.
- Audit log must capture tokenized prompt, model output hash, tool-call payload, response. Retention policy 2 years (legal).
- Want built-in rollback signal if refunds API returns 409/duplicate. Redwood fallback: surface human confirmation and attach original transaction id.

Sales/Procurement notes:
- Procurement timeline: procurement + security + legal aiming to close by 2026-04.
- Budget owner: Head of CX Ops (Marta Ruiz) — internal exec sponsor.
- Estimated ARR sits in $250k-$750k range depending on Dedicated vs Hosted.

Next steps (short):
- Confirm refunds API schema and shared dev sandbox creds (ACTION: Emberlane eng to send by 2026-03-10).
- Schedule 60m POC kickoff (Redwood SE Priya Nair) — aim week of 2026-03-15.
- Prep POC acceptance criteria: no duplicate refunds in 1000 simulated refunds, p95 latency < 600ms under 500rps, audit log integrity checks.

- "If it can't handle 3x traffic during promotions, we won't consider Hosted." — Lead SRE.
